messages:
customer-jones: Hi team — after moving our inference gateway to an on-prem egress-proxy (corporate Squid) our app starts getting 502/504 to the Redwood Private endpoint. Works fine from a laptop outside corp network. Anyone seen proxy-related breaks?

sara-support: hey @customer-jones — sorry you're hitting this. quick q: are you using an HTTP CONNECT proxy or a transparent inline proxy? and is your private deployment in 'no-internet' mode? :thinking_face:

customer-jones: CONNECT on :3128. Private control plane is reachable (we can hit the console), but model infer calls hang and then 502. We also saw occasional 401s. We tried from a vm with curl and saw TLS handshake errors sometimes.

cheng-eng: 2 quick repro commands please — run both from the gateway host: 
```
export HTTPS_PROXY=http://proxy.corp:3128
curl -v https://private-api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/predict -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" --max-time 20
```
and
```
openssl s_client -connect private-api.redwood-inference.internal:443 -servername private-api.redwood-inference.internal -proxy proxy.corp:3128
```
If the proxy is terminating TLS you might see cert presented by the proxy or a TLS error.

customer-jones: pasted curl output (sanitized): 
"* CONNECT proxy.corp:3128 HTTP/1.1"
"< HTTP/1.1 200 Connection established"
"* TLS handshake: sslv3 alert certificate unknown"
"* Closing connection 0"
then curl exits with 56.

eli-ops: that looks like the proxy is doing TLS interception AND the client does not trust the proxy CA. Two issues to check: 1) the proxy may be stripping Authorization headers for CONNECT or applying authz rules -> explains 401s; 2) proxy MITM cert not trusted -> TLS handshake failures.

customer-jones: ok we checked with our security team. The proxy injects a corporate CA. We added the CA to system store but the app runs in a JVM container — Java truststore wasn't updated. Could that cause intermittent 502s?

sara-support: yes — JVM relying on default cacerts would fail handshake unless you import the corp CA into the JVM truststore. Also some proxies rewrite chunks which can break streaming APIs (our streaming SSE/response chunk checks). For immediate repro, can you run curl with `-k` (insecure) to see if it bypasses the TLS failure (just for test)? Also try `-v --raw` to inspect if the proxy is buffering chunked responses.

customer-jones: ran `curl -k` and the 200 flows through but streaming is buffered and large responses arrive only after ~12s. Without proxy (direct) latency ~120ms. With proxy ~12s.

cheng-eng: buffering explains the latency. Many corporate proxies buffer full response before returning to client which kills streaming/latency SLOs. Two mitigation paths: 1) configure proxy to disable response buffering for the private-api host (bypass or passthrough rules), or 2) put a trusted egress gateway (NAT) for Redwood traffic that doesn't MITM and preserves CONNECT semantics.

customer-jones: how about DNS? The proxy resolves hostnames itself and uses its DNS — our DNS shows private-api resolves to internal VIP. Could proxy be resolving differently and hitting a wrong egress?

eli-ops: yes proxies can resolve upstream and route differently. Also ensure your firewall allows outbound TCP 443 to Redwood egress IPs. If you have allowlists, add our published egress IP ranges and destination hostnames. If in no-internet/airgapped mode, ensure the control plane + runtime have the required egress endpoints reachable (we'll list them).

customer-jones: can you list exact endpoints and ports to allow?

sara-support: sure — we'll DM the full list, but minimal quick checklist: 
- DNS A/AAAA for private-api.redwood-inference.internal -> resolve to your internal VIP (ok)
- TCP 443 outbound to Redwood runtime hosts (make sure proxy allows CONNECT to those hosts)
- Proxy must not strip `Authorization` and must forward `Host` and `Content-Length` headers.
- If proxy does TLS intercept: add proxy CA to JVM truststore, or configure proxy to `tunnel` CONNECT (no MITM) for our domains.

cheng-eng: also capture a small tcpdump of the failed flow and the proxy access logs showing the CONNECT and response codes. If you can include a short HAR or `curl -v` logs we can verify header stripping. Example headers we look for: `authorization: Bearer ...` present on the upstream request, and `transfer-encoding: chunked` preserved.

customer-jones: we grabbed squid logs — they show 200 on CONNECT then a 502 from upstream after some time. Proxy access log shows `Client IP - - [timestamp] "CONNECT private-api.redwood-inference.internal:443 HTTP/1.1" 200 0`. No obvious header logs yet.

eli-ops: 502 from upstream could be the proxy failing to reach the backend, or backend rejecting due to TLS issues. Two targeted tests to run from your proxy machine (shells):
```
# test direct TCP to backend
nc -vz private-api.redwood-inference.internal 443

# test whether proxy forwards auth header (replace TOKEN)
curl -v -x http://proxy.corp:3128 -H "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN" https://httpbin.org/anything
```
If httpbin shows the Authorization header then proxy preserves it. If not, that's the auth-stripping cause for 401s/billing breaks.

customer-jones: nc shows port open. curl to httpbin via proxy shows headers stripped (no Authorization). Security team says they remove credentials for some destinations.

sara-support: that matches the 401/billing symptom — requests hitting control plane without auth get rate-limited or rejected. Fix options: configure proxy exception for Redwood domains to preserve headers, or set up an egress NAT that bypasses proxy for traffic to our IP ranges.

oncall-bot: Incident checklist created: INC-2026. Tagging eng-oncall for routing rules if customer can't change corporate proxy.

customer-jones: thanks — we'll test two things today: 1) add corp CA to JVM truststore on the runtime container and 2) request proxy exception for header passthrough and no-buffering for private-api hosts. Will update with results.

cheng-eng: great — if you still see issues after that please attach: `curl -v` logs, squid access logs around the request, and a 30s tcpdump pcap. We can also run a quick replay from our side once you redact tokens.

customer-jones: update: adding CA to cacerts fixed handshake errors. Proxy team allowed header passthrough for our host and streaming is back to ~150ms. Closing for now, will reopen if we hit anything else. :relieved:
